properties.name: COSTING option (c): every part already exists and the whole thing runs in 0.08s — but it triggers on FAILING TOOL CALLS, and the overconfident-fix case Anthony described produces none
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-28, costing option (c) of the RCA brainstorm — "surface a known cause at the moment of the symptom".

═══ FOUR OF THE FIVE PARTS ALREADY EXIST ═══

**① RETRIEVAL WORKS, MEASURED ON THE CASE THAT ACTUALLY FAILED.** Searching the raw error string `git: 'remote-https' is not a git command` returns `fact:the-gh-merge-failure-is-snap-confinement-and-nobody-was-counting` as hit #1 at score 30.19. That is the exact root cause a session re-derived from scratch on 2026-08-22 while it sat in the graph. A second real symptom, `invalid GapCandidate: missing field suggested_depth`, returns the F-01 fix ChangeEvent at 39.76 with the root-cause rule second. **The information was always retrievable. Nobody called the search.**

**② A THRESHOLD SEPARATES SIGNAL FROM NOISE, on n=4.** Real symptoms with recorded causes: 30.19, 39.76. Plausible errors with nothing recorded: `connection refused ECONNREFUSED port 5432 postgres` → 13.35; `segmentation fault core dumped libssl undefined symbol` → 8.38. A cutoff near 20 fires on both true positives and neither control — a 2.3× margin.

**③ THE HOOK INFRASTRUCTURE IS INSTALLED.** `reflow2_init.py` already registers four hooks: SessionStart, PostToolUse on `mcp__reflow2__.*`, PostToolUse on `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`, and Stop. SessionStart already prints into the session's context, which is the surfacing mechanism this needs.

**④ LATENCY IS A NON-ISSUE, AND THAT WAS THE BIG UNKNOWN.** A COLD process — open the graph, initialize, run one search — is **0.08s**. Compare `graph_probe.py`'s own numbers, which exist because this constraint bit before: `loop_status` 22.6s, `loop_status since_export` 37.5s, `claim_report` 0.04s. Search sits with claim_report. **It can run inline; the async-probe pattern is not needed.**

═══ WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE BUILT — small ═══

Register PostToolUse on `Bash` (the tuple list already has the shape; today it matches reflow2 tools and edit tools only); read `tool_response`, which the payload carries and `loop_nudge.py` does not currently consume — it reads `tool_name` and `tool_input`; detect failure and extract a symptom string; search, threshold, format; suppress repeats within a session so a retried command does not fire the same hit every time.

═══ 🛑 AND THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST: IT REACHES THE WRONG HALF ═══

**This mechanism triggers on a FAILING TOOL CALL. The problem Anthony described produces none.** His words were that an agent "proposes a solution to an issue, then goes off and implements some solution, but it turns out that the solution only treated a symptom." That fix COMPILES. Its tests PASS. It ships green. There is no failing command anywhere for a PostToolUse hook to see.

So option (c) as costed solves the **2026-08-22 problem** — a recurring KNOWN error whose cause is already recorded and nobody searches, measured at 11+ occurrences of one issue — and does **not** solve the problem that prompted the brainstorm. Both are real. They are not the same problem, and one cheap mechanism should not be described as answering both.

⚠️ **COVERAGE IS 65%.** Of 192 defect-facts, 124 carry an error-like or quotable symptom that a string search could retrieve; 68 are abstract findings ("a finding can outrun its own data") that no error text will ever match. The abstract third is where the conceptual mistakes live — which is again the half Anthony is aiming at.

⚠️ **IT REACHES ONE HARNESS.** Hooks are Claude Code's. `dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only` is DECIDED and says a harness that cannot take the nudge is told so. Alex's Grok Build TUI cannot. **The second user — the one generating the field reports — would not get this.**

⚠️ **THE THRESHOLD IS CALIBRATED ON FOUR POINTS.** BM25 scores are unnormalised and scale with query length and corpus size, so 20 is a fitted guess, not a constant. Shipping it wrong in the permissive direction produces a hook that fires on everything, which is the wallpaper failure this project has already killed three times (unreviewed_ideas at 111 of 186, the undeclared-seam list, the unallocated-parts list). A real calibration set is a prerequisite, not a nicety.
